correctness.rationale: Backward Poisson spacings at a stationary observation time are independent rate-r exponentials. The sum of those spacings weighted by products of squared multipliers has mean 1/[r(1−m)] and converges in L¹. Conditional on the spacings and marks the independent Brownian increments give exactly the claimed Gaussian mixture, with D in the generator giving variance 2D per unit time. For uniqueness even from an invariant law of unknown moments, the common-noise difference equals the initial difference times a product with expected square exp(−r(1−m)t); truncate the finite initial difference and then use convergence in probability. The affine kernel preserves convex order in the previous clock and in the independent coefficient by conditioning; all stop-loss functions are 1-Lipschitz, hence pass to the L¹ limit. Jensen and the chord from zero to one give the exact coefficient endpoints; Poisson thinning gives the upper clock. Positive and negative half-power tests give the absolute moment and density directions; the latter is integrable since V≥E_0. Conditioning the normal MGF on V and testing exp(Dt²V) gives the common finite domain and sharp envelope. The generator recursion telescopes to the stated factorial product; finite exponential moments locally justify it. Jensen and B²≤B give the sharp kurtosis inequalities with the stated equality conditions; a mixture of the endpoint laws preserves m and interpolates E B². Independent exact replay at D/r=1 and m=1/4 substitutes E B^j=m^j, (1/2)^j/(j+1), or m into the recurrence. The three E X⁴ values are 512/15, 384/11, 128/3 with common E X²=8/3, giving kurtoses 24/5, 54/11, 6. This is a bounded check, not the proof of convex order. The frozen verification describes additional exact and seeded checks; its script was not executed.
